_about: The graph engine's constants, transcribed from raw/graph-code-notes.md. Each leaf names the identifier or the exact phrase it was read from (`id`, which tools/build_tokens.py checks is in the notes) and the notes section. Units: a `number` without a unit is in graph units (the 500-tall layout box) or is a factor; a `dimension` in px is screen pixels, which the engine keeps constant by multiplying with camera.inverse_z. `inferred: true` marks a value the notes mark as inferred or that this file had to interpret.

box.description: Height of the layout box in graph units; its width is 500 times the container's aspect ratio. The camera then fits this box to the screen.

log-base.description: Count axes and node size use log(count + 1) / log(4). The settings offer 2, 4 and 8.

collision-tolerance.description: Two nodes overlap when their centres are closer than 0.95 of touching.

collision-angle-step.description: Radians per spiral step on the first ring (2π/6); later rings divide it by the ring count.

collision-ring-step.description: Each full turn of the spiral grows its radius by this many node diameters.

collision-first-hit.description: On the first overlap the node jumps this many diameters out from the blocker's centre.

recenter-pad-x.description: Fraction of the viewport width kept clear on each side when fitting.

recenter-pad-y.description: Fraction of the viewport height kept clear above and below when fitting.

recenter-pad-min.description: The fit padding never goes below this.

recenter-zoom-divisor.description: The fit may zoom in at most to the fit-all zoom divided by this.

few-min.description: Smallest diameter, in graph units, when the graph has very few nodes.

few-max.description: Largest diameter when the graph has very few nodes.

many-min.description: Smallest diameter once the graph reaches the many-count.

many-max.description: Largest diameter once the graph reaches the many-count.

many-count.description: s = min(n / 150, 1) squared blends the two ranges.

halo-gap.description: A circle of radius r + 4 is erased (destination-out) before each node draws, so every node sits in a clear gap. Graph units, so the gap grows with zoom.

stroke.description: The ring of a result node.

stroke-width.description: Ring width of a node with no fill.

stroke-width-filled.id: width `4/z` if the node has a fill

fill-default.id: Default node colour if a fill array is empty

fill-saved.description: A saved article in no collection.

fill-seed.description: The orange of a saved search input: the first folder colour, which the notes infer and the screenshots match.

selected-fill.description: Disc drawn behind the selected node.

modified-ring.description: What sets a node modified was not read; the demo uses it for a node you moved, which is a guess.

icon-seed-scale.description: The seed glyph fills this fraction of the node's diameter.

icon-reveal.description: Icons, labels and edges wait until the node is this far through its entrance.

pie-start-angle.description: Degrees. A node in several collections is a pie, one slice per folder colour.

focus.description: An edge touching the hovered or selected node.

arrow-length.description: Arrowhead wing length in graph units, so the head grows with zoom.

arrow-angle.description: Radians either side of the edge.

arrow-gap.description: The tip stops this many graph units (halved) outside the target's diameter.

size.description: Constant on screen at every zoom.

weight-emphasis.description: The code names it for neighbours, but screenshots/search-split-light-hover-input.png shows neighbour labels at regular weight; the selected label is the one seen at 600.

hover-push.description: The notes say units; the label is drawn at constant screen size, so this reads it as screen px.

plate.description: The white plate under the hovered node's full title.

recede-opacity.description: Opacity of a node that is neither the focus nor one of its neighbours.

drag-threshold.description: A mouse up that moved less than this is a click.

wheel-zoom-speed.description: z' = max(min-zoom, z - deltaY × speed × z). The product leaves the wheel unattached; the demo attaches it.

camera.description: Recenter and any camera move without its own duration.

zoom.description: Toolbar zoom, key zoom and key pan.

spawn-min.description: Each node picks a random entrance time between spawn-min and spawn-max.

tween-min.description: Position and size changes: a random time per node, so the graph does not move as one block.

recede-min.description: Fading to and from the recede opacity, random per node.

frame-cap.description: Frames per second the loop allows at most.

easing-camera.description: The code names Penner's cubicEaseInOut; this is its standard CSS curve.

easing-tween.id: tween over **200 to 400 ms** (random per node), `cubicEaseInOut`

easing-spawn.description: Penner's backEaseOut as a CSS curve: the radius overshoots by about 10 percent, then settles.

stroke.description: The box names var(--color-cta), which a canvas cannot read, so its stroke is likely skipped; this takes the selection-box colour instead.
